Twelve migrants, including infant, drown as boats capsize off Greek islands

Reuters

19 October, 2026 03:00 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

Oct 19 (Reuters) – Twelve migrants drowned in two separate incidents off the Greek islands of Lesbos and Samos in the northeastern Aegean Sea on Monday, after their boats capsized as the coast guard chased them, authorities said.

Five men and one woman died after a speedboat carrying migrants from Turkey made a sudden manoeuvre and overturned roughly four nautical miles north of Samos, the Greek coast guard said.

Fourteen men survived and a search-and-rescue operation was under way. Authorities arrested one of the survivors, an Iranian national, on suspicion of migrant smuggling.

Show Full Article

Earlier, four men, one woman and an infant died when their boat collided with a Greek coast guard vessel and overturned off the area of Agrilia in Lesbos. Eight survivors were taken to hospital.

Authorities arrested a 37-year-old Turkish national who was among the eight survivors and identified him as the suspected smuggler and operator of the boat.

The government vowed “zero tolerance” towards migrant smugglers, whom it blamed for the deaths.

On the incident off Lesbos, Greece’s shipping minister Vassilis Kikilias said evidence so far indicated the speedboat struck the left side of a coast guard vessel with its bow, adding that the exact circumstances were under investigation.

“Our position is non-negotiable: zero tolerance for smugglers,” he said in a post on X.

Greece, for years a favoured gateway to Europe for migrants and refugees from the Middle East, Africa and Asia, was at the front line of Europe’s migration crisis in 2015-2016 and nearly 1 million people landed on its islands, mainly from Turkey.

It has since toughened its stance and has been accused by human rights groups of forcibly returning migrants and asylum-seekers on its sea and land borders, a practice it denies, saying its coast guard acts with full respect for human lives and rights.

(Reporting by Renee Maltezou and Antonis Pothitos; Editing by Lincoln Feast and Xevi Fontdegloria)

Australian lawmaker Helen Haines in critical condition after vehicle attack

Reuters

19 October, 2026 02:30 pm IST

Facebook

By Alasdair Pal SYDNEY, Oct 19 (Reuters) – Australian lawmaker Helen Haines was in a critical condition on Monday after being deliberately struck by a car outside her office in Wangaratta, northeast of Melbourne, police and Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said.

“All of our thoughts are with Helen, her family, her friends, her team, and her community at this extremely difficult time. We are praying for her full recovery,” Albanese told a news conference.

Victoria Police said a 43-year-old suspect had been arrested after Haines was struck by a car near her office in Wangaratta, around three hours’ drive northeast of Melbourne. Acting Superintendent Ashley Mason told a press conference there was no further threat to the public.

Show Full Article

Albanese said it was too early to determine the motive for the attack.

(Reporting by Shivani Tanna in Bengaluru, Alasdair Pal in Sydney; Editing by Kevin Liffey)

Putin approves Russian government reshuffle after parliamentary election, state media report

Reuters

19 October, 2026 01:01 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

(c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

MOSCOW, Oct 19 (Reuters) – Russian President Vladimir Putin has backed a government reshuffle proposed by Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin, state news agencies reported on Monday, citing the Kremlin.

“Along with a discussion on social and economic matters the prime minister proposed a number of personnel changes within the government to the head of state. These were endorsed by Putin,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov was quoted as saying by Russian news agencies.

The reshuffle follows a September parliamentary election which renewed the ranks of the State Duma lower house of parliament and comes as Russia is looking for new sources of growth amid a rising budget deficit, higher taxes and relatively high interest rates.

Show Full Article

The new ministers, who have not yet been publicly named, will be put forward for parliamentary approval, the Kremlin said, without giving further details.

(Reporting by ReutersEditing by Andrew Osborn )
